correctness.rationale: Encode each rule as a labeled edge, with terminal rules going to one sink. Words are bounded by complete path count. Removing the r edges out of the start leaves budget e=p-r and at most M(e) continuations per head, counting the sink's empty continuation as one. Matching parallel chains give the maximum integer product over positive parts summing to p. M(p) increases strictly for p>=2 by increasing a part of a maximizing composition of p-1. At equality all p rules lie on complete paths and the word labels are collision-free. The case e=0 gives a single terminal layer; e=1 is impossible for p>=2 since at most p-1 paths would result. For e>=2 each maximizing suffix head must use every remaining edge by strict monotonicity. Distinct heads would have to reach each other, using an outgoing edge of the other, contradicting acyclicity. Thus there is one head per layer, inductively. The p=1 case requires exactly one terminal production at the start. Merging ones, replacing a part b>=5 by 3 and b-3, and replacing three twos by two threes give strict improvements; splitting a four into two twos preserves equality and yields the listed maximizing compositions. Mixed-radix labels yield exactly each exponent 0 through M(p)-1 once even over a unary alphabet. For the cover, the necessary count bound and the interval produced at the least feasible p coincide, giving the stated inverse and bounded additive remainder.
residual_risks: The finite graph check is narrower than the advertised full rectangle: its loop range(2,min(p+2,6)) excludes larger vertex counts at low p (e.g. p=1,n=3). This reporting limitation does not affect the analytic proof and the scripts are not relied on as exhaustive evidence for the theorem.
The inverse is for a cover that may generate a strict superset, not necessarily minimum cost for exact generation.

evidence: Hetzl–Shadman use the same arbitrary-block production cost and prove general and binary cover NP-completeness. Hetzl–Wolfsteiner bound finite linear grammars by 2^(p-1). The dissertation reports logarithmic production-size generation for arbitrary finite unary languages in longest word length.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Decision hardness, a looser count upper bound, and order-of-growth generation for a broader class do not settle the exact cover complexity of consecutive unary intervals or characterize capacity extremizers.

checked_sources: Hetzl–Shadman grammar model and Hetzl–Wolfsteiner Lemma 7
value.rationale: The exact maximum and structural equality theorem address a natural resource question in the regular-cover model: how many distinct words a production budget can buy, and what must happen in an optimal description. The collision-free unary realization turns that maximum into an exact inverse for a natural test family, substantially sharpening the older cardinality bound rather than merely restating integer-break arithmetic.
residual_risks: Arbitrary-length labels cost one production; results need not transfer to single-letter rules or symbol cost. The exact cover corollary is for consecutive lengths, not arbitrary finite unary or larger-alphabet languages of the same cardinality.
